body:
STORYATLAS DISPOSITION — ACCEPT D3 AS A HARD ARTIFACT LAW; AMEND “VISIBLE” TO MEAN ACCOUNTED, DISTINGUISHABLE, AND INSPECTABLE AT THE CURRENT LEVEL OF DETAIL.

Identity: `codex-storyatlas-root`. I inspected the current storymodel4s `view` seam and the StoryAtlas ownership/build contract. This is design feedback only: no module, CLI, schema, or implementation is authorized here.

The important current fact is that the view layer already refuses one common conflation, but not yet the whole D3 requirement. `FeatureChannelState` distinguishes `NotRequested`, `Unresolved`, `Missing`, and `SidecarRequired`; `FeatureObservationPlacement` deliberately carries no numeric value and points to checked sidecar material. That is a good layer-materialization contract. It is not yet a per-target accounting contract for measured, imputed, ineligible, failed, and excluded values. StoryAtlas therefore cannot infer “absent” from “no placement.” The compiler must supply the distinction.

D3: ACCEPT, WITH THREE ORTHOGONAL STATE FAMILIES

1. Claim grounding/status: explicit or supported inference, retained alternative, hypothesis, rejected/unresolved. An accepted interpretive claim with no evidence is primarily a model error, not a missing-feature glyph.
2. Feature/acquisition state: measured(value), missing(reason), imputed(value, method/receipt), ineligible(reason), unresolved/failed, excluded, and not requested.
3. Display state: visible mark, bundled at this level of detail, filtered by an explicit policy, or off-projection. Display suppression must never masquerade as scientific absence.

Those families need separate fields and separate visual grammar. “No node,” “no measurement,” and “not drawn at this zoom” are different facts.

I would phrase the hard law as follows:

    For every requested channel, the compiled artifact declares its target universe and eligibility policy, accounts for every eligible target, and preserves the composition of measured, missing, imputed, ineligible, unresolved/failed, and explicitly excluded states through aggregation and level of detail. No renderer may infer one of those states from silence.

The level-of-detail clause matters. A book-scale view cannot draw one missingness icon per token and remain usable. D3 should require semantic observability, not permanent clutter: a coarse region may show a coverage/status composition bar, hatch, or table; selecting or descending exposes exact target states. Counts and denominators must conserve across descent. A measured numeric zero remains measured. A region with zero eligible targets cannot advertise “100% support.”

A single discriminating fixture should contain: a measured zero; a measured nonzero; an imputed value numerically equal to a measured value; an eligible missing value; an ineligible target; a failed/unresolved target; and one observation deliberately bundled by level of detail. At token and aggregate scales, textual twins and non-colour marks must distinguish them. Delete one eligible row without updating the accounting inventory and compilation must refuse. Remove only the imputation receipt and the imputed state must become unresolved, never measured.

D1: HARD ACCEPT STANDOFF

The exact source bytes are an observation, not a serialization inconvenience. Inline markup can be an explicitly lossy convenience export, but it cannot be canonical identity. Span support remains offsets into a checksummed immutable source atlas; discontinuous support stays discontinuous rather than becoming a hull.

D2 + D5: TWO ARTIFACT CLASSES, ONE BUNDLE

Do not make HTML an interchange format, and do not make rendered geometry part of model identity. I recommend a versioned, manifest-bounded directory bundle with two owned layers:

- Scientific/interchange layer, owned by storymodel4s: exact source artifact, canonical model JSON, typed sidecar references or included sidecars, build/provenance receipt, schema/version identifiers.
- Publication/report layer, owned by StoryAtlas: declared `ViewSpec`, renderer-neutral compiled-view identity or packet, projection contract, textual twins, layout/renderer receipt, and self-contained HTML/SVG preview.

A minimal text profile could look like:

    manifest.json
    source/source.txt
    model/model.json
    sidecars/...                 optional, all manifest-bound
    views/codex.json             or canonical packet digest + textual twin
    views/discourse-atlas.json   or canonical packet digest + textual twin
    preview.html
    receipt.json
    exports/brat/...             optional, with export-loss.json

The manifest binds every path by media type, role, byte length, checksum, schema version, and required/optional status. A deterministic archive can come later; the directory is easier to inspect and stream.

Round-trip law belongs to the scientific layer: decode into the unchecked/draft domain, revalidate, and recover the same canonical content identities and exact source bytes. The preview is a report. It owes deterministic reproduction from model + `ViewSpec` + layout inputs, complete provenance, and textual-twin equality; it does not owe `parseHtml(render(model)) == model`. A lossy exporter owes a machine-readable loss manifest naming dropped relation/status/evidence/feature distinctions and binding both source and model checksums.

Ownership should preserve ADR 0002: storymodel4s owns schemas, validated artifacts, compiled view packets, identities, status, evidence, and receipts; StoryAtlas owns pagination, layout, lowering, HTML/SVG, and the user-facing preview orchestration. storymodel4s must not depend on StoryAtlas. One command may orchestrate both once arbitrary-text Stage 1b exists, but the dependency direction does not change.

D4: CODEX + ATLAS, NOT ONE HEROIC OVERLAY

The first preview should contain two canonical faces in one self-contained, script-free report:

1. Narrative Codex: exact DOM text, local span annotations, hierarchy gutters, local relations, feature/missingness track, and typed portal endpoints for nonlocal links.
2. One declared story-scale Discourse Atlas: hierarchy, threads, landmarks, and selected relation family, with its `ProjectionContract` printed beside it.

Each Atlas mark links by stable identity to its Codex evidence anchor and inspector table; each Codex annotation links back. In a script-free report this can be ordinary fragment navigation rather than pretending to be the full synchronized application. Cross-page causal/world-time relations should use paired portals plus a relation inventory or a separate declared projection. A many-page arrow and a single all-purpose node-link hairball are both false economy.

The MVP should show one quantitative feature at a time, source/model/build receipts, explicit horizon/context/status, and a compact coverage ledger. More projections can be additional static plates, each with an honest contract; they must not share unexplained distance semantics.

TEXT-FIRST WITHOUT A TEXT-ONLY CONTAINER

Implement the first profile for ASCII text, but do not bake “the source is always source.txt” into the abstract manifest. A later film profile will bind edition/rendition/stream/axis identities and may carry access disposition plus external media checksums rather than redistributing media bytes. It must never serialize credentials or silently substitute subtitles for unavailable film. This is a reason for typed artifact roles in the manifest, not a reason to expand the first CLI into film work.

MINIMUM ACCEPTANCE COURTS

- emitted source bytes equal input bytes exactly;
- canonical model decode -> validate preserves content identities;
- concatenated Codex text fragments equal the source exactly;
- every selectable interpretive mark resolves to Address, evidence/upstream claims, status, and provenance;
- requested-channel accounting distinguishes zero/missing/imputed/ineligible/failed/excluded and conserves under level of detail;
- same model + view + layout inputs produce byte-identical renderer-neutral packets and declared deterministic outputs;
- preview has no network dependency, external font, hidden credential, or scientific inference;
- every lossy export carries a bound loss manifest;
- HTML is explicitly a report, never accepted as the authoritative model on re-import.

Bottom line: the owner should receive one inspectable bundle and one command, but the bundle must preserve two truths: the model is canonical standoff science, and the HTML is a reproducible evidentiary report over that model. D3 is the gate that prevents a polished preview from becoming a prettier form of missing-data corruption.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not inspect every current codec for bundle completeness, choose concrete wire-field names, create a bead, alter the accepted mockup candidate, or authorize the arbitrary-text provider path.
